SQL Overview

1. SQL in Apache Ignite
  • Ignite includes a distributed SQL engine based on Apache Calcite (Ignite 2 uses H2);
  • You can run standard ANSI SQL queries — SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE;
  • Queries are automatically distributed across cluster nodes — each node processes its local partitions;
  • SQL tables and key-value caches are two views of the same data — you can use both interchangeably;
2. DDL (Data Definition Language)
  • Create tables and indexes with standard SQL: 
    CREATE TABLE Person (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR,
    age INT,
    city VARCHAR
) WITH "cache_name=PersonCache,template=partitioned,backups=1";

CREATE INDEX idx_person_city ON Person (city);

ALTER TABLE Person ADD COLUMN email VARCHAR;

DROP TABLE Person;
  • The WITH clause passes cache configuration parameters (cache name, template, backups, affinity key, etc.);
3. DML (Data Manipulation Language)
  • -- Insert
INSERT INTO Person (id, name, age, city) VALUES (1, 'Alice', 30, 'NYC');

-- Update
UPDATE Person SET age = 31 WHERE id = 1;

-- Delete
DELETE FROM Person WHERE city = 'NYC';

-- Merge (upsert)
MERGE INTO Person (id, name, age, city) VALUES (1, 'Alice', 32, 'Boston');
4. Querying via Java API
  • SqlFieldsQuery — the primary query API; returns rows as lists of fields: 
    SqlFieldsQuery query = new SqlFieldsQuery(
    "SELECT name, age FROM Person WHERE city = ?"
);
query.setArgs("NYC");

try (QueryCursor<List<?>> cursor = cache.query(query)) {
    for (List<?> row : cursor) {
        String name = (String) row.get(0);
        int age = (int) row.get(1);
    }
}
5. JDBC and ODBC Access
  • Ignite provides a JDBC thin driver for connecting external tools (DBeaver, IntelliJ, custom apps): 
    String url = "jdbc:ignite:thin://192.168.1.10:10800";
Connection conn = DriverManager.getConnection(url);

Statement stmt = conn.createStatement();
ResultSet rs = stmt.executeQuery("SELECT * FROM Person WHERE age > 25");
  • ODBC driver is also available for non-Java clients;
6. Limitations
  • DML inside transactions requires TRANSACTIONAL atomicity mode (or the ALLOW_DML_INSIDE_TRANSACTION flag for ATOMIC caches);
  • DDL operations (CREATE TABLE, CREATE INDEX) are not transactional;
  • Subqueries and correlated subqueries have performance implications in distributed mode;
  • Non-colocated joins must be explicitly enabled and are slower than colocated joins;
